run.procedureSummary: Feed: add each cycle's feed row to chambers 1-6, ignoring capacity, PUPAL chambers included. Overflow: go through chambers 1 to 6 in order; any amount over capacity is cut back to capacity and the excess is added to the next chamber before that chamber is checked, so it can overflow in turn; excess from chamber 6 goes to the loss tally. Check (uses the quantities after overflow, one test per chamber): a LARVAL chamber with quantity >= its upper mark becomes PUPAL; a PUPAL chamber with quantity <= its lower mark becomes LARVAL; otherwise the state stays the same. Metabolism (states as set by this cycle's check; all amounts worked out from the quantities before anything moves): a LARVAL chamber loses floor(q/4) to the tally; a PUPAL chamber loses floor(q/2), which goes to chamber i-1, or to the tally for chamber 1; there is no overflow pass afterwards, so a chamber can stay over capacity until the next cycle's overflow step. Moult: if the line total after metabolism is strictly greater than 38, every chamber becomes floor(q/2) and the removed mass goes to the tally. Report after cycle 5. I used a short Python script at C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\sim.py and checked cycle 1 by hand.

openPoints.point: Check order relative to marks: which quantity the check uses
openPoints.assumption: The check uses the quantities after this cycle's overflow. Each chamber gets one test per cycle based on its state at the start of the check, so a chamber cannot flip twice in one cycle.

openPoints.point: Meaning of 'routinely' in the PUPAL return rule
openPoints.assumption: I read it as the normal deterministic rule with no extra condition: a PUPAL chamber at or below its lower mark always returns to LARVAL.
Metabolism uses the states set by this cycle's check. All loss and transfer amounts come from the quantities before metabolism, then they are applied at the same time.
floor(q/2) moves to chamber i-1, ignoring capacity, and chamber 1's amount goes to the tally. A chamber left over capacity stays that way until the next overflow step, so there is no extra overflow.
I always round down (floor) on non-negative integers: quarter loss, half reabsorption and moult halving.
The moult fires only when the line total is strictly greater than 38. A total of exactly 38 (end of cycle 5) does not fire it. The total is measured after metabolism.
The moult changes quantities only; it does not change states. No new check runs after the moult.
Overflow is a single pass from 1 to 6. Excess passed into a chamber is counted before that chamber is tested, so cascades happen within the pass, and nothing flows backward.
